about: LittleBot's offline trivia bank (littlebot/games/voice/trivia.py). Each question: q, a (the right answer), wrong (three wrong answers), fact (one short line), cat, lvl (easy | medium | hard). Options are shuffled when asked.

questions.q: How many days are in a leap year?
questions.fact: The extra day, February 29th, comes about every four years.

questions.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.fact: Honeybees build their honeycomb cells as hexagons.

questions.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.fact: A newborn joey is only about the size of a jellybean.

questions.q: Which month has the fewest days?
questions.fact: February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year.

questions.q: How many colours are usually counted in a rainbow?
questions.fact: Isaac Newton picked seven: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

questions.q: What is the hardest natural substance?
questions.fact: Diamond is pure carbon, the same element as the graphite in a pencil.

questions.q: How many keys does a standard piano have?
questions.fact: That's 52 white keys and 36 black keys.

questions.q: How many minutes are in a full day?
questions.fact: 24 hours times 60 minutes makes 1,440.

questions.q: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.fact: Close to a billion people grew up speaking Mandarin.

questions.q: Which letter doesn't appear in the name of any U.S. state?
questions.fact: Z sneaks into Arizona, X into Texas and J into New Jersey.

questions.q: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, which word stands for the letter K?
questions.fact: Alpha, Bravo, Charlie: the alphabet was adopted in the 1950s so letters are never misheard on the radio.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Iron oxide, basically rust, gives Mars its red colour.

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.fact: Insects have six legs, so spiders aren't insects: they're arachnids.

questions.q: What gas do plants take in from the air to make their food?
questions.fact: They give off oxygen as they make food from sunlight.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.fact: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

questions.q: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.fact: More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

questions.q: What is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.fact: The femur, your thigh bone, is about a quarter of your height.

questions.q: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.fact: The next closest, Proxima Centauri, is over four light-years away.

questions.q: Which part of a cell holds most of its DNA?
questions.fact: Stretched out, the DNA in one of your cells would be about two metres long.

questions.q: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fact: Light crosses the 150 million kilometres in about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

questions.q: What is the most common gas in Earth's air?
questions.fact: Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of the air we breathe.

questions.q: Which element has the atomic number 1?
questions.fact: Hydrogen is the most common element in the universe.

questions.q: At sea level, at what temperature in Celsius does water boil?
questions.fact: That's 212 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: He stepped onto the Moon in July 1969, with Buzz Aldrin right behind him.

questions.q: Which ancient people built the great pyramids of Giza?
questions.fact: The Great Pyramid was the tallest human-made structure for about 3,800 years.

questions.q: In which year did the Titanic sink?
questions.fact: It sank on its very first voyage, after hitting an iceberg.

questions.q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.fact: It hangs in the Louvre museum in Paris.

questions.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.fact: It was opened on November 9th, 1989.

questions.q: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.fact: It was dedicated in New York Harbor in 1886.

questions.q: Genghis Khan founded which empire?
questions.fact: It became the largest connected land empire in history.

questions.q: Whose expedition was the first to sail all the way around the world?
questions.fact: Magellan died on the way; Juan Sebastián Elcano brought the ship home in 1522.

questions.q: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.fact: She won two, one in physics and one in chemistry.

questions.q: Who was the first emperor of Rome?
questions.fact: Julius Caesar was never emperor; his heir Augustus was.

questions.q: In which year was the Magna Carta sealed?
questions.fact: King John agreed to it at Runnymede, near London.

questions.q: What is the capital of France?
questions.fact: The Eiffel Tower was built there for the 1889 World's Fair.

questions.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.fact: The Pacific is bigger than all of Earth's land put together.

questions.q: On which continent is Kenya?
questions.fact: Kenya is named after Mount Kenya, its highest mountain.

questions.q: What is the capital of Japan?
questions.fact: Kyoto was Japan's capital for over a thousand years before Tokyo.

questions.q: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra was built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.q: What is the smallest country in the world?
questions.fact: It sits inside the city of Rome and is smaller than many city parks.

questions.q: Which river is usually called the longest in the world?
questions.fact: Some measurements put the Amazon just ahead, so the race is close.

questions.q: Which river flows through London?
questions.fact: The Thames is about 346 kilometres long.

questions.q: What is the largest country in South America?
questions.fact: Brazil borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.

questions.q: Mount Everest sits on the border of Nepal and which other country?
questions.fact: Its peak is about 8,849 metres above sea level.

questions.q: Which is the driest non-polar desert on Earth?
questions.fact: Parts of the Atacama, in Chile, get almost no rain at all.

questions.q: Counting its overseas territories, which country has the most time zones?
questions.fact: With islands all over the world, France spans 12 time zones.

questions.q: How many players does a soccer team have on the field?
questions.fact: That includes the goalkeeper.

questions.q: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.fact: The five rings stand for the parts of the world joined by the Games.

questions.q: In which sport do you score a touchdown?
questions.fact: A touchdown is worth six points.

questions.q: What sport is played at Wimbledon?
questions.fact: Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world, from 1877.

questions.q: In basketball, how many points is a shot from behind the arc worth?
questions.fact: The three-point line came to the NBA in 1979.

questions.q: About how long is a marathon?
questions.fact: The official distance is 42.195 kilometres, or 26.2 miles.

questions.q: In tennis, what is a score of zero called?
questions.fact: One theory says it comes from l'oeuf, French for egg, because a zero looks like one.

questions.q: How many holes are played in a standard round of golf?
questions.fact: St Andrews in Scotland made 18 holes the standard.

questions.q: In snooker, how many points is the black ball worth?
questions.fact: Pink is 6, blue 5, brown 4, green 3, yellow 2 and each red 1.

questions.q: Which country won the first FIFA World Cup, in 1930?
questions.fact: Uruguay hosted that first World Cup too.

questions.q: How many minutes long is a regulation NBA game?
questions.fact: That's four quarters of 12 minutes each.

questions.q: In Toy Story, what is the cowboy's name?
questions.fact: Toy Story, from 1995, was the first fully computer-animated feature film.

questions.q: What is the name of the snowman in Frozen?
questions.fact: Sven is the reindeer, and Kristoff is his best friend.

questions.q: What colour is Shrek?
questions.fact: Shrek is based on a picture book by William Steig.

questions.q: In Finding Nemo, what kind of fish is Nemo?
questions.fact: Real clownfish live safely among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones.

questions.q: Which school of witchcraft and wizardry does Harry Potter attend?
questions.fact: Durmstrang and Beauxbatons are rival schools in the stories.

questions.q: In Star Wars, who is Luke Skywalker's father?
questions.fact: Darth Vader was once the Jedi Anakin Skywalker.

questions.q: Which Pixar movie has a house lifted into the sky by thousands of balloons?
questions.fact: Up came out in 2009.

questions.q: Which 1993 movie brought dinosaurs back to life in an island park?
questions.fact: It was based on Michael Crichton's novel.

questions.q: What was Walt Disney's first feature-length animated film?
questions.a: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.fact: It came out in 1937.

questions.q: In the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz, what colour are Dorothy's slippers?
questions.fact: In the original book, the slippers were silver.

questions.q: Which film won the very first Oscar for Best Animated Feature?
questions.fact: The award was first given in 2002.

questions.q: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.fact: A standard bass guitar usually has four.

questions.q: Which of these is a brass instrument?
questions.fact: Brass players make the sound by buzzing their lips into the mouthpiece.

questions.q: How many musicians play in a quartet?
questions.fact: A string quartet is two violins, a viola and a cello.

questions.q: Which band sang Hey Jude and Let It Be?
questions.fact: The Beatles came from Liverpool, England.

questions.q: Who is known as the King of Pop?
questions.fact: His album Thriller is one of the best-selling albums ever.

questions.q: Which instrument is Yo-Yo Ma famous for playing?
questions.fact: He started playing the cello at age four.

questions.q: Which singer is called the Queen of Soul?
questions.fact: Her hit Respect topped the charts in 1967.

questions.q: Which Queen song begins with the line "Is this the real life?"
questions.fact: It runs almost six minutes and has no chorus.

questions.q: How many symphonies did Beethoven finish?
questions.fact: He wrote some of them, including the Ninth, while almost completely deaf.

questions.q: Who composed The Four Seasons?
questions.fact: It's a set of four violin concertos from the 1720s.

questions.q: What does a conductor usually hold to lead an orchestra?
questions.fact: Some conductors, like Pierre Boulez, preferred to use just their hands.

questions.q: Which fruit is dried to make raisins?
questions.fact: Dried plums are called prunes.

questions.q: What is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.fact: Avocados are a fruit; botanists even call them berries.

questions.q: Which vegetable often makes people cry when they cut it?
questions.fact: Cutting an onion releases a gas that stings your eyes.

questions.q: Which country is pizza as we know it from?
questions.fact: The Margherita pizza is said to be named after an Italian queen.

questions.q: Which nut is marzipan made from?
questions.fact: Marzipan is mostly ground almonds and sugar.

questions.q: What is tofu made from?
questions.fact: Making tofu is a bit like making cheese, but with soy milk.

questions.q: Which country does paella come from?
questions.fact: Paella comes from Valencia, on Spain's east coast.

questions.q: Which fruit wears its seeds on the outside?
questions.fact: A strawberry has about 200 seeds on its skin.

questions.q: Which spice is the most expensive by weight?
questions.fact: Saffron is the tiny threads picked by hand from crocus flowers.

questions.q: Which pasta's name means "little worms" in Italian?
questions.fact: Spaghetti means little strings.

questions.q: What is sushi rice traditionally seasoned with?
questions.fact: The word sushi comes from an old word meaning sour, from the vinegared rice.

questions.q: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.fact: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857.

questions.q: Which leaf is on Canada's flag?
questions.fact: The maple leaf flag was first raised in 1965.

questions.q: What is the largest city in Canada?
questions.fact: Toronto's CN Tower was the world's tallest free-standing structure for over 30 years.

questions.q: How many provinces does Canada have?
questions.fact: There are three territories too: Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut.

questions.q: What is Canada's national winter sport?
questions.fact: Lacrosse is Canada's national summer sport.

questions.q: What is Canada's two-dollar coin nicknamed?
questions.fact: The one-dollar loonie is named after the loon on it.

questions.q: Which territory, created in 1999, is Canada's newest?
questions.fact: Nunavut means "our land" in Inuktitut.

questions.q: In which province is Banff National Park?
questions.fact: Banff, from 1885, is Canada's oldest national park.

questions.q: Which is Canada's only officially bilingual province?
questions.fact: Quebec's only official language is French.

questions.q: Which Canadian invented the game of basketball?
questions.fact: He invented it in 1891, using peach baskets as the hoops.

questions.q: Which Canadian doctor shared a Nobel Prize for discovering insulin?
questions.fact: He shared the 1923 Nobel Prize in Medicine.

questions.q: Which country has the most lakes in the world?
questions.fact: By many counts, Canada has more than half of all the natural lakes on Earth.

questions.q: What does www stand for in a web address?
questions.fact: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the web in 1989.

questions.q: Which company makes the iPhone?
questions.fact: The first iPhone came out in 2007.

questions.q: Which company makes the Android phone software?
questions.fact: Android versions were once named after desserts, like Cupcake and KitKat.

questions.q: What do we call the little pictures people send in text messages?
questions.fact: Emoji comes from Japanese: e means picture and moji means character.

questions.q: What does CPU stand for?
questions.fact: The CPU is the part of a computer that runs the instructions.

questions.q: How many bits are in a byte?
questions.fact: With 8 bits, a byte can hold 256 different values.

questions.q: Who founded Microsoft with Paul Allen?
questions.fact: They started Microsoft in 1975.

questions.q: Which small, cheap computer, named after a fruit, is LittleBot's brain?
questions.fact: The first Raspberry Pi came out in 2012.

questions.q: Who is often called the first computer programmer?
questions.fact: In the 1840s she wrote a program for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.

questions.q: What does USB stand for?
questions.fact: USB first appeared in 1996.

questions.q: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.fact: The S in HTTPS stands for secure.
